title: PECARN Paediatric Head Injury Rule — CT Decision
subtitle: children <18 y, GCS 14–15, within 24 h of head trauma

sources.title: STG & EML Paediatric Hospital Level, 2025-2029 cycle (updated Mar 2026)
STG & EML Primary Healthcare, 8th ed. 2024 (updated Sept 2026)
Kuppermann N et al. PECARN head injury rules. Lancet 2009;374:1160-70

cells: GCS 14 or other altered mental status, OR palpable skull fracture
GCS 14 or other altered mental status, OR signs of basal skull fracture
Non-frontal scalp haematoma, LOC ≥5 s, severe mechanism, or not acting normally per parent
Any LOC, vomiting, severe mechanism, or severe headache
Observation vs CT (ciTBI ≈0.9%) — CT more likely if several findings, worsening, age <3 months, parental preference

items.t: MVC with ejection, death of another passenger or rollover
Pedestrian or unhelmeted cyclist struck by a motorised vehicle
Fall >0.9 m (3 ft) if <2 y; >1.5 m (5 ft) if ≥2 y
Head struck by a high-impact object
TBI: CT within 0–6 hours; refer all children with TBI
Major-injury indicators include decreased level of consciousness; children <2 years with these require admission
Severe TBI = GCS <9 → refer to a specialised centre
Applies only to GCS 14–15; GCS ≤13 → CT/referral regardless
ciTBI = death, neurosurgery, intubation >24 h or admission ≥2 nights for TBI
Isolated vomiting as the only finding (≥2 y): observation is reasonable
Suspected non-accidental injury: rule does not apply — act on safeguarding
